newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF head sees six pct Russian growth by 2000.
newsitem.headline: IMF head sees six pct Russian growth by 2000.

text.p: The head of the International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday Russia was likely to have six percent annual growth by the turn of the century.

"At the turn of the century, Russia should have growth -- one of the highest rates in Europe -- six percent or so," IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus told students at an international affairs institute.
Camdessus said that Russia's new government appeared committed to reforms needed to bring the Russian economy back to growth.

Official statistics have shown growth of under one percent in the years to January and February after years of declining national output, though many economists say state methodology was changed without announcement.
There is also a growing shadow economy. The government is predicting two percent growth for this year.
Camdessus said growth was in reach but not guaranteed.
"Russia risks being mired in this economic no man's land between a centrally planned system and a fully functioning market economy," he said.
Camdessus is in Moscow for talks with senior Russian ministers on resuming disbursements of a $10 billion three-year loan and agreeing an economic programme for 1997 to be backed by the loan.
Camdessus also said now was the time for the international community to resume lending to Russia.
